title: Workflows, agents, and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Two makerspace handlers both use a model and the tools check_calendar, book_slot and send_email. Handler 1: the model labels the message "booking" or "question", and the code then runs the fixed steps for that label. Handler 2: the model gets the message and the tool list, the code runs whichever tool the model names and feeds back the result, and this repeats until the model says it is done. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Handler 1 is a workflow and handler 2 an agent, because only in handler 2 does the model choose the steps
Both are agents, because both call a model and run tools
Handler 1 is an agent, because the model's label decides which steps run
Both are workflows, because in each one the code is what runs the tools

items.stem: Your code is `while steps < 10: reply = call_model(messages, tools); if no tool requested: break; result = run_tool(reply); messages.append(result); steps += 1`. After each tool result, who decides what runs next, the model or the code, and does the `steps < 10` cap change that?

A job runs at 2 a.m.: for each student whose safety training expires within 7 days, it reads their record, writes a one-paragraph reminder with a model, and sends it. The sponsor's model budget is small. Which design is best for keeping cost down?

options.text: One agent with query, draft and send tools, choosing its own order each night
Plain code looping over all students, with a model call to judge who needs a reminder
Plain code that selects students by date, then one agent per student to draft and send
Plain code that selects students by date, with one model call per reminder

items.stem: Handling one request costs 2 model calls as a fixed workflow, or on average 5 model calls as an agent. Assume every call costs $0.002 and the assistant gets 10,000 requests a month. How many more dollars per month does the agent design cost than the workflow?
Which of these makerspace requests is the best fit for an agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Tell a student which of our three laser cutters is free tomorrow
Work out why a student's recent booking attempts keep failing
Cancel a student's booking and email them the change
Summarise the safety rules for the vinyl cutter from its manual

items.stem: A design routes every request with one model call that labels it. 95% of requests get a fixed workflow of 2 more model calls; the other 5% go to an agent that takes 5 model calls on average. What is the average number of model calls per request, counting the routing call?
